title: Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill 2014
short_title: Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill 2014

speeches.speaker: David Feeney
speeches.brief: Supported a technical Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill 2014 stemming from a 2009 Labor review, but condemned the government for switching veterans' pension indexation to CPI only, a change affecting some 280,000 veterans, and for axing $870 seniors supplements and $217 annual payments to children of war veterans.

speeches.speaker: Philip Ruddock
speeches.brief: Declared that the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Industry Code Penalties) Bill 2014, the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill 2014, and the International Tax Agreements Amendment Bill 2014 were referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

speeches.speaker: Warren Snowdon
speeches.brief: Supported the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill, recounting the 2009 review that led to a $17.4 million commitment to implement 96 of 108 recommendations, and explained the bill fixes a technical barrier preventing retrospective recalculation of permanent impairment compensation.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Nikolic
speeches.brief: Supported the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill, drawing on his 30 years in the Australian Army and Australia's longest ever military engagement in Iraq and Afghanistan, and said the changes would make compensation more agile without disadvantaging any veteran.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Supported the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill after visiting the soldier recovery centre at Gallipoli Barracks in her electorate, explaining the bill fixes a technical barrier so the commission can retrospectively recalculate permanent impairment compensation following a 2009 review.

speeches.speaker: Nickolas Varvaris
speeches.brief: Supported the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill, noting more than 26,000 Australians served in Afghanistan and about 17,500 in Iraq, and said the Department of Veterans' Affairs serves over 310,000 veterans and their families nationally.

speeches.speaker: Ewen Jones
speeches.brief: Supported the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill, saying no veteran would be disadvantaged by the new compensation calculation method, and highlighted Townsville's more than 4,000 DVA clients and the 3rd Brigade's centenary this year.

speeches.speaker: Gai Brodtmann
speeches.brief: Supported the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill 2014, a technical amendment letting the commission retrospectively recalculate permanent impairment compensation after review, noted Labor's 2012 to 2013 budget commitment of $17.4 million to implement 96 of the review's 108 recommendations, and praised the veterans' charity Soldier On.

speeches.speaker: Melissa Price
speeches.brief: Supported the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill, which lets the commission retrospectively apply new permanent impairment compensation methodology for beneficial or neutral outcomes only, traced the RSL's formation from 1916, and highlighted a Geraldton project recreating an 11th Battalion trench linked to the battalion's landing at Anzac Cove on 25 April 1915.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: Argued that the bill implements a Labor review and removes a technical barrier to retrospectively recalculating some veterans' permanent impairment compensation. Criticised proposed changes to veterans' indexation and payments, and raised difficulties obtaining service records and departmental advice, urging improved support for veterans.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: Summed up support for the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill 2014, saying it will allow retrospective recalculation of certain permanent impairment compensation for ADF members and former members without disadvantaging anyone. Said the measure addresses a technical barrier identified during reviews and commended the bill.

acts.title: Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Act 2014
